title: October Jobs Report: Payrolls Rise 165,000, Beating Forecasts; Unemployment 4.1%
dek: The Bureau of Labor Statistics reported at 8:30 a.m. ET that October nonfarm payrolls rose 165,000 against forecasts of about 59,000 to 65,000. The unemployment rate was 4.1%.
author: Meridian Newsroom

image.alt: Black-and-white photograph of an automatic ticker apparatus on the New York Stock Exchange trading floor
image.credit: Library of Congress via Wikimedia Commons

keyPoints: The BLS reported at 8:30 a.m. ET on Friday, Nov. 6 that nonfarm payrolls rose 165,000 in October; the unemployment rate changed little at 4.1% (BLS).
The Dow Jones forecast was 59,000 jobs (CNBC); Business Insider cited a 65,000 consensus. Either way the gain beat expectations.
Average hourly earnings rose 0.4% on the month and 3.1% from a year earlier, against estimates of 0.3% and 2.9% (CNBC).
Professional and business services added 70,000 and health care 42,000; transportation and warehousing added 25,000 (CNBC; BLS).
CME FedWatch odds for a quarter-point hike at the Dec. 8-9 FOMC meeting were 76.8% after the report (CNBC).
body:
## The release: 165,000 jobs

The Bureau of Labor Statistics published the October Employment Situation at 8:30 a.m. ET on Friday. Nonfarm payrolls rose 165,000, and the unemployment rate changed little at 4.1%. The BLS said the gain was higher than the average monthly gain of 48,000 over the prior 12 months. Business Insider's live recap reported that August and September were revised up.

## Against expectations

CNBC cited a Dow Jones consensus of 59,000 jobs. Business Insider cited 65,000 and a steady 4.2% unemployment rate. Both forecasts were beaten, and the unemployment rate came in below the 4.2% forecast.

## Wages and sectors

Average hourly earnings rose 0.4% on the month and 3.1% over the year. Professional and business services led the gains, followed by health care and transportation. Economists quoted by CNBC described the breadth of hiring as broader than the health-care-led gains of recent months.

## Rates

The report came as the Federal Reserve weighs whether to resume raising rates. CME FedWatch odds for a December quarter-point hike rose to 76.8% after the release, according to CNBC. Goldman Sachs Asset Management's Lindsay Rosner said the number removed a reason for the Fed to wait.

## Market reaction

Stocks steadied after the release. By 10:46 a.m. ET, Yahoo Finance's live page showed the Dow up 0.1%, the S&P 500 up 1% and the Nasdaq Composite up 1.9%, after a Thursday sell-off that had pushed the Nasdaq into correction. Economists quoted by Business Insider said the report removed a barrier to a December rate increase. Goldman Sachs Asset Management's Lindsay Rosner said continued tightening in the labor market gives the Fed room to raise rates without hurting its employment mandate. Bellwether Wealth's Clark Bellin said the stronger report could help sentiment, which had been hurt by worries about the AI build-out after the midterm elections.

## Caveats

The 59,000 and 65,000 forecasts come from different sources, so the size of the beat depends on which consensus is used. Business Insider also reported that August and September were revised up. Wage growth of 3.1% year over year will be compared with inflation data due next week.

## What is not yet known

The BLS release is the official source for these figures. The market close is not covered here, and the index levels above are intraday readings with as-of times.

marketImpact.summary: A stronger-than-forecast report points to a firmer labor market and higher odds of a December rate increase. That is a headwind for rate-sensitive stocks and supports Treasury yields, while the report also steadied sentiment after Thursday's tech sell-off.
marketImpact.timeframe: Friday, Nov. 6, from the 8:30 a.m. ET release through the midday session

tickers.rationale: A stronger report lifts December hike odds, which CME FedWatch put at 76.8% after the release (CNBC).
Rate-hike odds weigh on rate-sensitive blue chips; the Dow was roughly flat at 10:46 a.m. ET (Yahoo Finance).

Inflation data due Tuesday, which will show whether 3.1% wage growth beats inflation (Business Insider).
